display.purpose: The one headline on a screen that has one — the Top 10 masthead over its hero art. Never twice on a screen.

title.purpose: The subject of the screen: a game's name on its own page, a collection's name, a profile's name.

heading.purpose: Section headings inside a scroll, and the largest step a card is allowed.

body.purpose: Reading copy. Synopses and long-form review text; the reason the scale bottoms out at 15px rather than 14.

bodyStrong.purpose: Body size promoted: a row's title, a button's label, a tab's label.

caption.purpose: Subtitles under a title; the second line of a list row.

micro.purpose: Counts, timestamps, and classification labels. Set in caps only when it counts or classifies.

shadows.name: object
shadows.purpose: Depicted physical objects only — the game case and the disc. Wraps face and spine as one object. Android elevation 12.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Available on Card and Poster but unused across the dark interface, where it is invisible. Earns its keep in light mode. Android elevation 3.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.purpose: Reserved for a future lifted surface. Not currently applied. Android elevation 8.

shadows.name: header-tail
shadows.purpose: Drawn, not cast, across the bottom fifth of the floating header. A transparent view has nothing to cast from. 0.14 alpha in light mode.

motion.name: fast
motion.purpose: Press-in. The sink under a finger.

motion.name: normal
motion.purpose: Press-out and default state transitions. Image cross-fades run 220–280ms.

motion.name: slow
motion.purpose: The longest anything is allowed to take. Above ~250ms a feed starts to feel sluggish.

motion.name: press-scale
motion.purpose: Default scale while held. Tighter targets go to 0.94; icon buttons to 0.90. Runs on the UI thread via Reanimated so it survives a busy JS thread.

motion.name: spring-layout
motion.purpose: The dock's selection pill moving between items. The only spring in the system.

breakpoints.name: content-max
breakpoints.purpose: MaxContentWidth. The single column centres and stops growing past this, so a tablet or the web build stays readable without becoming a desktop layout.

ratios.name: poster
ratios.purpose: Portrait box art. Every poster in the app.

ratios.name: hero
ratios.purpose: Landscape key art. Every hero and banner.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single most important action on a screen. At most one per screen.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; min-height: 46px; padding: 11px 16px; background: #FAFAFA; color: #0A0A0A; border: 1px solid #FAFAFA; border-radius: 10px; font: 600 15px/22px system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 140ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), background 140ms; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #FFFFFF; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #FAFAFA; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The default for everything. Raised dark fill with a hairline outline; pressed it steps one fill lighter.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; min-height: 46px; padding: 11px 16px; background: #1C1C1C; color: #FAFAFA; border: 1px solid #262626; border-radius: 10px; font: 600 15px/22px system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 140ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), background 140ms; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #232323; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: scale(0.97); background: #282828; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #FAFAFA; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-count { min-width: 22px; padding: 1px 5px; border-radius: 6px; background: #282828; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Destructive actions. Red type on a dark fill, never a red slab — a filled red button is the loudest object possible on a near-black screen.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-danger"><svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"><path d="M3 6h18M8 6V4h8v2M19 6l-1 14H6L5 6"/></svg>Delete</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; min-height: 34px; padding: 7px 12px; background: #1C1C1C; color: #EF4444; border: 1px solid rgba(239,68,68,0.33); border-radius: 10px; font: 500 13px/18px system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 140ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), background 140ms; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: #232323; } .ds-btn-danger:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #EF4444; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Icon Button
components.description: The same rectangle with equal sides, so an overflow or add glyph at the end of a row of labelled buttons reads as one of them. Square, never round.
components.html: <button class="ds-icon-btn" aria-label="More"><svg width="19" height="19" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor"><circle cx="5" cy="12" r="1.8"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1.8"/><circle cx="19" cy="12" r="1.8"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-icon-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 40px; height: 40px; background: #1C1C1C; color: #A3A3A3; border: 1px solid #262626; border-radius: 10px; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 140ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), background 140ms, color 140ms; } .ds-icon-btn:hover { background: #232323; color: #FAFAFA; } .ds-icon-btn:active { transform: scale(0.90); background: #282828; } .ds-icon-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #FAFAFA; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Sort Pill
components.description: A single choice from a fixed set. Selection is one step lighter in fill, edge and label — never a colour change.
components.css: .ds-sorts { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; } .ds-sort { padding: 8px 12px; background: #1C1C1C; color: #A3A3A3; border: 1px solid #262626; border-radius: 10px; font: 600 11px/14px system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 140ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), background 140ms, border-color 140ms, color 140ms; } .ds-sort:hover { color: #FAFAFA; } .ds-sort:active { transform: scale(0.94); } .ds-sort.is-selected { background: #282828; border-color: #383838; color: #FAFAFA; } .ds-sort:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #FAFAFA; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Slate fill, hairline edge, 16px text so iOS does not zoom on focus. Errors move the outline and the footnote, never the fill.
components.css: .ds-input { display: block; width: 100%; min-height: 48px; padding: 10px 12px; background: #141414; color: #FAFAFA; border: 1px solid #262626; border-radius: 12px; font: 400 16px/22px system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, sans-serif; transition: border-color 220ms; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #6E6E6E; } .ds-input:hover { border-color: #383838; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #FAFAFA; } .ds-input[aria-invalid="true"] { border-color: #EF4444; }

components.name: Card
components.description: One step off the page, no shadow, no border. The tonal step is the whole separation strategy.
components.css: .ds-card { padding: 16px; background: #141414; border-radius: 18px; color: #FAFAFA; } .ds-card-title { font: 700 20px/26px system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-card-meta { margin-top: 4px; color: #6E6E6E; font: 600 11px/14px system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.04em; }

components.name: Tab Bar
components.description: Scrollable underline tabs. Selected is full-strength label over a 2px near-white underline; the contrast is brightness, which survives sitting over artwork.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; gap: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid #262626; padding: 0 8px; } .ds-tab { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 12px 16px; background: none; border: 0; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; color: #6E6E6E; font: 600 15px/22px system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: color 140ms, border-color 140ms, transform 140ms; } .ds-tab:hover { color: #A3A3A3; } .ds-tab:active { transform: scale(0.94); } .ds-tab.is-active { color: #FAFAFA; border-bottom-color: #FAFAFA; } .ds-tab:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #FAFAFA; outline-offset: -2px; } .ds-tab-count { min-width: 18px; padding: 1px 5px; border-radius: 999px; background: #EF4444; color: #FFFFFF; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; }

components.name: Score Pill
components.description: The 0–100 score as a tinted block: verdict colour at 13% fill, full strength on the edge and numeral. A three-stop ramp (Moss / Amber / Ember), not fifteen colours.
components.html: 925821
components.css: .ds-scores { display: flex; gap: 8px; align-items: center; } .ds-score { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 44px; height: 44px; border-radius: 12px; border: 1px solid currentColor; font: 800 20px/1 system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-score.is-positive { color: #4ADE80; background: rgba(74,222,128,0.13); } .ds-score.is-neutral { color: #F5A524; background: rgba(245,165,36,0.13); } .ds-score.is-negative { color: #EF4444; background: rgba(239,68,68,0.13); }

components.name: Cover Tile
components.description: Box art, title, year. No card, no surface, no pill. The unit a chart or curated shelf is built from; an optional rank sits in muted micro beside the art rather than in a badge.
components.html: 2Hollow Knight: Silksong2025
components.css: .ds-cover-tile { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; width: 220px; text-decoration: none; transition: transform 140ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-cover-tile:active { transform: scale(0.96); } .ds-cover-rank { width: 14px; text-align: right; color: #6E6E6E; font: 600 11px/14px system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-cover-art { flex: none; width: 62px; aspect-ratio: 2 / 3; border-radius: 8px; background: linear-gradient(160deg, #2A2A2A, #141414); } .ds-cover-caption { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; min-width: 0; } .ds-cover-title { color: #FAFAFA; font: 600 15px/22px system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-cover-year { color: #6E6E6E; font: 500 13px/18px system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, sans-serif; }

narrative.overview:
The room is dark so the boxes are the only thing lit. GameLog's interface is a near-black room — Ink (#0A0A0A) walls, Slate (#141414) shelving you sense rather than look at — and everything with colour in it belongs to a game, not to the app. Box art is the content on nearly every screen, so the chrome's job is to be a frame that never argues with what it frames.

The temperament is quiet and exacting. Confidence here is expressed through consistency and tight detail, not through statements: every interactive rectangle is the same rectangle at the same radius, every selected thing is exactly one step lighter than an unselected one, every hero image fades into the page on the same ramp. Nothing is loud unless it is artwork. The components are refined and restrained — low contrast, generous padding, controls that ask for attention only when you go looking for them — while the game case, the one object the app renders as a physical thing, is allowed to be as present as a real boxed copy on a shelf.

The system replaced a blue-accented predecessor, and that predecessor is the named anti-reference. A blue button beside orange key art read as a second, louder piece of artwork; the whole point of moving to a monochrome scale was to stop the interface competing for the eye it is supposed to be directing.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black, monochrome chrome; every hue on screen is borrowed from a game.
Separation by tonal step plus a hairline edge — never by fill colour.
One rectangle for every control: 10px radius, hairline outline.
Emphasis is a change in value, not in hue: selected is one step lighter.
Interface is flat; depicted objects cast real shadows.
The system typeface is the OS's own; hierarchy comes from size and weight.

rules.name: The Borrowed Colour Rule
rules.body: Every colour on a screen belongs to a game, not to the app. Amber, Ember and Moss are the only exceptions, and each is licensed by a single job — ratings, danger, success. A fourth app-owned hue is a bug. A control may wear one of the three only when the control's meaning is that colour's job: Favourite takes Amber, Playing takes Moss; Wishlist, Played and Share do not. The test is not "is this state important" but "would the reader lose information if it were grey".

rules.name: The Value-Not-Hue Rule
rules.body: Selection, emphasis and primacy are expressed by moving one step lighter — Graphite → Iron for the fill, Seam → Ridge for the edge, Ash → Bone for the label. Never by changing hue. This is what makes a row of five sort pills stay quiet while still showing which one is on.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: No custom typeface ships. Hierarchy is built from size and weight alone, and a new step must be justified against the eight that exist rather than added beside them.

rules.name: The Caps-For-Counting Rule
rules.body: micro set in caps is for labels that count or classify — 12 GAMES, COMMUNITY, THIS MONTH, RANKED. It is never used for a sentence, and sentence-case micro is never used for a classification.

rules.name: The Bleed Rule
rules.body: Hero artwork always reaches both edges and always runs under the header. A hero inset by its container's padding is a hero that has been turned into a picture of a hero.

rules.name: The Object Rule
rules.body: If it depicts a physical object, it casts a shadow. If it is interface, it does not. There is no third case, and "this card feels flat" is not one.

rules.name: The One Rectangle Rule
rules.body: Every control is Radius.control. If you are reaching for Radius.pill on something tappable, you are about to make a tag look like a button.

dos: Do express every selected, active or emphasised state as one step lighter — Graphite → Iron, Seam → Ridge, Ash/Smoke → Bone.
Do give every interactive rectangle Radius.control (10px) and a hairlineWidth outline in Seam.
Do let hero artwork bleed to both edges and run under the transparent header, cancelling container padding with a negative margin.
Do end scroll containers with Spacing.seven (48px) of bottom padding.
Do use withAlpha(colour, 0) as a gradient's transparent stop, never the keyword transparent — Android interpolates through black and leaves a grey bruise across the middle of the ramp.
Do reach for a tonal step before a border, and a border before a shadow.
Do keep the count badge on a tab in Ember and the count badge inside a button recessed and colourless. One means "unseen"; the other means "how many".
donts: Don't introduce a coloured accent. No brand hue on buttons, links, tabs or selected states — the blue-accented predecessor is the named anti-reference. Only Amber (ratings), Ember (danger) and Moss (success) may carry colour, and each only for its one job.
Don't make a control pill-shaped. Radius.pill means "this is not a control" — progress tracks, count badges, avatars, metadata chips. Shape is the only thing left telling a tag apart from a button.

Don't put the game case anywhere but a game's own dedicated page. Not in a feed, a search result, a list tile, a comment, a notification or a widget — those use flat cover art. Diluting it destroys the one moment in the app that feels physical.
Don't give interface a drop shadow. Cards, buttons, sheets and docks are flat; only depicted objects cast.
Don't stretch landscape key art into a portrait poster slot. Poster crops with cover and falls back to a lettered placeholder — that fallback is what the missing cover is for.
Don't add a ninth step to the type scale, or a second typeface, without first failing to express the idea with the eight weights and sizes that exist.
